unanimous.note: Unanimous derives from Latin unanimus: un = one and anim = mind, spirit.

unbridgeable.note: Unbridgeable is un + bridge + able with the final e dropped.

unbridled.note: Unbridled is un + bridle + ed with the final e dropped.

unexpected.note: Unexpected is un + expect + ed; expect derives from ex + spect = look, not nex = bind.

uninhabited.note: Uninhabited is un + inhabit + ed; inhabit belongs to habit = dwell.

unobstructed.note: Unobstructed is un + obstruct + ed; struct = build.

unpalatable.note: Unpalatable is un + palatable; lat = bring is unrelated.

unsubstantiated.note: Unsubstantiated is un + substantiate + ed with the final e dropped; anti = old is unrelated.

untamed.note: Untamed is un + tame + d; med = middle is unrelated.

upbraid.note: Upbraid is historically up + braid, not up + bray; the ECDICT lemma upbray is erroneous.

uprising.note: Uprising is up + rise + ing, not a free compound with the malformed ECDICT lemma uprise.

uptodate.note: Fixed phrase normally written up-to-date; retain as a lexical item rather than splitting into function-word roots.

urbanite.note: Urbanite is urban + ite; ban = prohibit is unrelated.

viral.note: Viral is derived from virus + al with the base shortened to vir before the suffix.

vitamine.note: Vitamine is a vitamin spelling variant; vitamin was coined from vita = life and amine, not vita + mine.

waggon.note: Waggon is a wagon spelling variant; retain the free-word base.

walnut.note: Historically a foreign nut, but wal is not a useful modern reusable root; retain walnut as a lexical item.

wednesday.note: Wednesday is a weekday name retained as an independent lexical item.

welfare.note: Welfare is the transparent historical compound well + fare; wel is only a spelling variant.

wollongong.note: Australian place name; do not extract the English adjective long from its spelling.

workman.note: Transparent compound; man = person, not hand or stay.
